summary: In Greek mythology, Amphion (Ancient Greek Ἀμφίων) is a name borne by several men. The atlas node amphion-pella is the Argonaut — son of Hyperasius (son of Pelles) from Pellene, or in some notices from Macedonian Pella — who sails with his brother Asterius; he is kept strictly distinct from Amphion the Theban wall-builder and from Amphion of Minyan Orchomenus.

sections.heading: Argonaut son of Hyperasius
paragraphs: Apollonius, Valerius Flaccus, and Hyginus place Amphion among the Argonauts with his brother Asterius, sons of Hyperasius of Pellene (Pausanias knows the Achaean city); rival notices name Hypso as mother or Hippasus as father. The atlas residence label follows the Macedonian Pella notice used at entry while the catalogues keep the Pellenean Hyperasid identity.

Homonym care: not Amphion twin of Zethus who builds Thebes' walls (amphion); not Amphion king of Orchomenus father of Chloris (amphion-orchomenus); not the Epeian commander at Troy. The atlas id is the Hyperasid Argonaut alone.
